# FAQ-009 Engineering FAQ #9

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the recommended spindle warm-up procedure for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) and why is it required?
A: The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 27 minutes. Background: A controlled warm-up minimizes thermal gradients in the spindle, reducing runout drift during the first pieces after machine start. Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach a stable thermal state reduces scrap risk and tool wear caused by changes in geometry during production start-up. Example procedure: Power the machine control, run the spindle at low to medium rpm per OEM guidance until the elapsed warm-up reaches the specified time, then proceed with normal cut verification. Records to keep: log the machine ID (EQ-P1-L3-CN03), start time, end time, operator initials, and any deviations from the warm-up sequence. Reference change control or setpoint updates in ECN-2026-004 where applicable.

Q: What is the required coil cooling water flow for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02), and what are the consequences of not meeting it?
A: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Background: Induction heater coil cooling is critical to prevent coil overheating and damage to insulation. Rationale: Maintaining at least the minimum flow preserves coil life and prevents unplanned downtime due to coil failure. Example operational checks: Verify flow indication on the heater panel and confirm coolant supply is stable before charging the heater. Records to keep: record the equipment ID (EQ-P2-L1-IH02), flow readings when taken, operator name, and any corrective actions if flow falls below the minimum. See SOP-P2-L1-03 for permitted response steps and ECN-2026-004 for any recent coil or system modifications.

Q: Which lubricant part number is approved for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01), and how should it be applied?
A: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is CFW-LUB-961. Background: The radial ring rolling mill requires a controlled lubricant to manage metal-to-metal contact and thermal conditions at the tooling interface. Rationale: Using the specified lubricant ensures compatibility with seals, bearings, and process temperatures, and it aligns with maintenance and procurement records. Application guidance: Apply per the lubrication points defined in the mill lubrication map and follow the quantity guidance from the mill OEM or maintenance procedure. Records to keep: maintain a lubrication log that includes equipment ID (EQ-P1-L2-RR01), lubricant part number (CFW-LUB-961), batch/lot number, application date, technician initials, and any observations. Cross-reference SOP-P3-L3-02 for related lubrication audit requirements and ECN-2026-004 if lubricant spec was revised.

Q: What lubricant is specified for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) and what controls govern its use?
A: The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709. Background: Shot blast cabinets have peripheral components that require specific lubricants to protect bearings and guideways from abrasive media and dust ingestion. Rationale: Specifying CFW-LUB-709 limits cross-contamination risk and ensures replacement lubricant meets filtration and viscosity properties compatible with the cabinet environment. Application and control: Apply during scheduled maintenance windows and capture lubrication events in the cabinet maintenance record. Records to keep: document cabinet ID (EQ-P3-L3-SB01), lubricant part number (CFW-LUB-709), date of use, lot number, technician, and any subsequent observations about performance or leakage. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-02 for maintenance steps and ECN-2026-004 for any related equipment changes.

Q: What lubricant is approved for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) and what traceability is required?
A: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is CFW-LUB-278. Background: Cabinets in the Hot Forge area are exposed to elevated ambient conditions and abrasive recycle streams; lubricant choice must support those conditions and facility contamination controls. Rationale: Using CFW-LUB-278 provides consistent performance and allows procurement and maintenance to trace lubricants used in the Hot Forge area for failure analysis. Traceability and records: maintain procurement receipts and maintenance logs that show the equipment ID (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), lubricant part number (CFW-LUB-278), supplier batch/lot, date applied, technician initials, and any analytical results if oil sampling is performed. Consult SOP-P2-L1-03 and SOP-P3-L3-02 for oil handling, storage, and disposal controls; record any changes via ECN-2026-004.

Related documents: ECN-2026-004, SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P3-L3-02

Document control note: Keep lubrication and warm-up logs in the equipment folder and link entries to the applicable ECN when changes to procedure or part numbers occur.
